meta.about: Incorporated in 2016, Go Digit General Insurance Ltd provides motor, health, and other insurances[1]
meta.keyPoints: Business Overview:[1] GDGIL is a digital full stack insurance company which designs products, distributes and provides customer experience for non-life insurance products. Company offers motor insurance, health insurance, travel insurance, property insurance, marine insurance, liability insurance and other insurance products
pros: Company has delivered good profit growth of 45.1% CAGR over last 5 years
cons: Stock is trading at 2.85 times its book value
Though the company is reporting repeated profits, it is not paying out dividend
Company has a low return on equity of 10.5% over last 3 years.

bull.point: Fairfax to acquire 60.72% of IDBI Bank and contribute its Digit General/Life stakes to IDBI at market price -> captive bancassurance channel; Kamesh Goyal says it significantly strengthens Digit's distribution. Stock +22% in <1 month to mid-Oct.

Promoter holdco (GDISPL) amalgamation lifts Fairfax's direct stake from ~35% effective to 57.28% (fully diluted); shares issued at Rs375.10, a premium to market - signals Fairfax commitment; 100% FDI now allowed so Fairfax has headroom to infuse capital.
Consensus sees EPS +13% FY27 and +36% FY28; Emkay models CoR improving 108.9% -> 105.0% FY27-29 and ROE 12.8% -> 16.5%.
Strong capital: solvency 2.43x (Q1FY27), CRISIL AA- (watch developing).
Reserving looks conservative: Motor TP accident years FY19-FY23 show 22-41% favourable development vs original estimate; ex-TP book 6-13% favourable.

Ind AS (mandatory from 1-Apr-2026) optics are better: FY26 Ind AS PAT Rs778cr vs IGAAP Rs544cr; Ind AS net worth Rs7,610cr vs IGAAP Rs4,586cr, so P/B on Ind AS is ~3.3x not 5.3x; Ind AS CoR 103.0% (FY26).
Domestic MFs accumulating: MF holding 7.0% (Sep-25) -> 11.11% (Sep-26); ICICI Pru MF and ABSL MF bought Peak XV's block exits.
Management expects Motor OD loss ratio to stabilise from Q2FY27 after car-portfolio corrective action; growth pullback described as deliberate (crop/volatile business).

bear.point: Persistent underwriting losses: IGAAP combined ratio 107.4% (FY23), 108.7% (FY24), 109.3% (FY25), 110.7% (FY26), 112.4% (Q1FY27). FY26 U/W deficit Rs866cr vs investment income Rs1,591cr - profits are an investment-income story.
Q1FY27: GWP -8.4% YoY, first market-share decline since inception; motor share 6.25% -> 5.6%; PAT -38%.
Highest expense structure among large private insurers: FY26 EoM 40.47% of GDP vs 30% cap (2nd worst general insurer); breached again in Q1FY27, forbearance sought from IRDAI.
Valuation still rich for a sub-13% ROE: ~50x trailing P/E, 5.3x P/B (IGAAP); sharpely flags 'expensive vs industry P/B' and continuous EPS downgrades.
Emkay: competitive intensity across segments plus Digit's high-opex model make profitable growth difficult; no clear moat (since IPO).
Motor concentration: 69% of GDP in FY26 (CRISIL); Jun-26 Supreme Court Shishupal ruling on Motor TP not reserved for additionally by mgmt.
Stock below Rs272 IPO price 29 months after listing; -24% over 1 year; FIIs cut holding 8.23% -> 6.58% in Sep-26 quarter.

quarterlyKpis.commentary: Pre-IPO quarter; LR not separately disclosed (H1FY24 LR 66.5%). Inv. income derived H1 473 less Q2 248.
Cyclone Michaung (Dec-23) and other cat losses; NEP derived 9M 5,115 less H1 3,132.
First quarter post IPO (May-24 fresh issue Rs1,125cr lifted solvency to 2.17x). Booked Rs19.5cr loss switching to higher-yield securities.
First quarter under IRDAI 1/n for long-term policies (from 1-Oct-24); PAT 2.8x YoY; stock +16% on results day (best day since listing). Booked Rs254cr govt health inward RI.
First tax-paying quarter (~14% rate). Fire grew ~40% on hard RI pricing; low retention from fire/inward RI.

Floods ~Rs30cr in OD; new-2W growth (Rs451cr vs 334cr) cost Rs53cr / ~2pt CoR under IGAAP (5-yr commission upfront, premium earned over 5 yrs). OD market share 6.2% (record). Post-tax DAC Rs1,708cr; ~Rs710cr to unwind in H2. NEP derived (9M 6,113 less Q1, Q3); inv. income derived FY 1,591 less other quarters.

GDPI +20.9% but GWP +8.7% as Rs254cr govt health inward RI not renewed (Rs38cr). 2W collected premium +47% (Rs668cr) cost Rs84cr / 3.9pt IGAAP CoR. First motor quota-share (funds-withheld) and health cession cut NWP. New wage code one-off Rs7cr. Accumulated losses fully wiped.

IGAAP PBT +49% YoY. Health inward RI not renewed (~Rs252cr), GWP ex-health +18.8%. 2W new business Rs556cr vs 365cr (~3.5pt EoM impact). Middle-East war: unrealised loss Rs54cr at Mar-26. Started OD corrective action (Feb-26).

Statutory (IGAAP) PAT -38% YoY (86.4 vs 138.3cr); PBT -28% (115.5 vs 160.7). Drivers: (1) deliberate de-growth in soft market - GWP -8.4% (non-renewal of group health & crop inward RI; ex these ~-2%), CV -27%, fire -37% vs industry -28%; (2) loss ratio 73.3% vs 70.3% driven by private-car OD (75.9% vs 69.3%) and a large fire claim; IGAAP CoR 112.3% vs 108.6%; (3) effective tax ~25% vs ~14% (accumulated losses exhausted in FY26); (4) chose not to harvest equity gains; higher equity allocation (9.5%) cost ~Rs14cr interest income. Management KPI (PAT with DAC) only -5% (190 vs 200cr); Ind AS PAT rose to 372 from 325cr on MTM and discounting. Motor market share fell to 5.6% from 6.25%. EoM above regulatory limit; forbearance sought. Stock hit all-time low ~Rs259 (-7.8%) on 24-Jul-26; Emkay TP 270 (Reduce), Jefferies TP 380.

timeline.title: Incorporation
timeline.detail: Go Digit General Insurance incorporated in Pune (CIN ...2016PLC167410); holding company Go Digit Infoworks Services (GDISPL) incorporated 21-Dec-2016. Founder Kamesh Goyal, ex-CEO of Bajaj Allianz General and Bajaj Allianz Life, ex-Allianz.

timeline.title: Fairfax-led seed capital
timeline.detail: Fairfax (via FAL Corporation) and promoters fund the start-up; promoters invested >$140mn over 2017-18 (Inc42); reported ~$47mn June-2017 round.

timeline.title: IRDAI registration
timeline.detail: IRDAI Registration No. 158 dated 20-Sep-2017; operations start Oct-2017 with motor-led digital distribution.

timeline.title: First external round ($84mn) incl. Virat Kohli & Anushka Sharma
timeline.detail: A91 Partners, Faering Capital, TVS Capital invest ~$84mn at ~$870mn post-money; Kohli/Sharma invest ~Rs2.5cr. Month approximate.

timeline.title: Unicorn
timeline.detail: Raises Rs135cr (~$18mn) from existing investors at $1.9bn valuation - first Indian unicorn of 2021.

timeline.title: $200mn round at $3.5bn
timeline.detail: Led by Faering Capital; new investors Sequoia Capital India and IIFL Alternate Asset Managers.
timeline.impact: Peak private valuation (~Rs26,000cr), above current market cap

timeline.title: Jasleen Kohli appointed MD & CEO
timeline.detail: Founding member Jasleen Kohli MD & CEO w.e.f. 20-Apr-2022; Kamesh Goyal moves to Non-Executive Chairman (nominee of GDISPL).
timeline.impact: Founder retains strategic control as chairman

timeline.title: Last motor TP tariff revision
timeline.detail: MoRTH-notified motor TP premiums last revised effective 1-Jun-2022; no hike since (management: "5 years, no TP hike"). IRDAI has sent recommendations for a hike.
timeline.impact: TP loss ratios exposed to wage/legal inflation

timeline.title: First DRHP filed
timeline.detail: DRHP filed Aug-2022 (FY22 GWP 5,268cr, net expense ratio 38.7%).

timeline.title: SEBI puts IPO in abeyance; papers returned Jan-2023
timeline.detail: Concern over Employee Stock Appreciation Rights plan; ESAR 2018 converted to ESOP 2018 (Mar-2023) and DRHP refiled Mar/Apr-2023.

timeline.title: IRDAI Expense of Management regulations
timeline.detail: EoM regulations (2023, consolidated 2024) set overall EoM caps and freed commission structures; industry commissions rose and players chased group health/crop to meet limits (per management).
timeline.impact: Digit EoM ratio 39-42% exceeds limits; shareholders absorb excess (Rs324cr FY25, Rs469cr FY26)

timeline.title: IRDAI penalty Rs1cr
timeline.detail: IRDAI order dated 2-May-2024: Rs1cr penalty for non-intimation of change in conversion ratio of holding-company CCPS (Sec 26, Insurance Act).
timeline.impact: Minor; governance flag around holding structure

timeline.title: IPO at Rs272; listed 23-May-2024
timeline.detail: Issue Rs2,614.65cr: fresh Rs1,125cr + OFS 5.48cr shares (Rs1,489.65cr), almost all by promoter GDISPL (54,755,614 sh) plus three small individual sellers. Anchor Rs1,176.6cr (Fidelity, Goldman Sachs, ADIA, SBI MF, ICICI Pru MF, etc.). Subscribed ~9.6-10x. Listed at Rs281 BSE (+3.3%), closed ~Rs302-306 day 1.
timeline.impact: Solvency rose from 1.61x to 2.17x; net proceeds Rs1,064.7cr for solvency

timeline.title: Record high ~Rs372 (Jun-24); FY25 high Rs398.4
timeline.detail: Stock hit Rs372 on 12-Jun-2024 Q4 results day; FY25 intra-year high Rs398.40 / low Rs278.50 (post-issue report, NSE).

timeline.title: IRDAI 1/n accounting for long-term policies
timeline.detail: From 1-Oct-2024 applicable long-term premium recognised on 1/n basis; acquisition cost still expensed upfront.
timeline.impact: Lowers reported GWP (FY25 -137cr, FY26 -303cr) and raises IGAAP CoR (+0.7pt FY25, +1.8pt FY26); no profit impact

timeline.title: Services from holding company discontinued
timeline.detail: At IRDAI's request, service arrangements between GDISPL and the insurer stopped Nov-2024.

timeline.title: Analyst Day
timeline.detail: Management sets out KPI framework (NEP-based CoR with DAC; no guidance).

timeline.title: 52-week high Rs381.4 (24-Sep-2025)
timeline.detail: Rally into GST cut on vehicles (22-Sep-25) boosting new-vehicle sales.

timeline.title: Scheme: amalgamation of GDISPL into Go Digit
timeline.detail: Board approves 19-Dec-2025 merger of holding company Go Digit Infoworks; its shares split among FAL (Fairfax), Oben Ventures and Kamesh Goyal; ~11.69 lakh new shares (~Rs43cr) issued at Rs375.10; promoter holding +0.03%. timeline.title: Accumulated losses wiped; becomes full taxpayer
timeline.detail: Q3FY26: all accumulated losses wiped; FY26 tax rate 13.8%, 25.2% from FY27.

timeline.title: Ind AS (IFRS 17-like) results published; IRDAI mandate from 1-Apr-2026

timeline.title: Supreme Court homemaker-income ruling (Shishupal)

timeline.impact: Motor TP severity risk; may reduce future reserve releases

timeline.title: Q1FY27: PAT -38%, all-time low

Distribution economics reset: IRDAI's proposed commission caps and ~1/3 EoM cut (from Jan-2027) would compress acquisition costs and broker/POSP payouts - positive for COR, disruptive for broker-led growth.

Underwriting losses are structural (industry COR 111-113%, UW loss Rs 45k cr FY26); returns depend on investment income (~Rs 48k cr FY25), so yields/MTM drive ROE; disciplined large privates earn 15-18% ROE vs ~6% for the industry.
Private share gains continue as PSUs (34% incl. AIC/ECGC) struggle with wage costs and sub-1.5x solvency; capital infusion, merger or repricing possible.

Accounting and regulatory transition: Ind AS 117, RBC solvency, 100% FDI and Bima Sugam raise comparability, capital efficiency and competition over FY27-29; reported metrics (IGAAP vs Ind AS) will be noisy.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Go Digit General Insurance (standalone, IGAAP, ₹ crore). Base year FY26A from company disclosures. Valuation on Ind AS book (fairer economics) via residual income.
assumptions._gwpWhy: FY27: management is 'soft by choice' and prepared for flat-to-negative growth until Mar-27 (Q1 GWP -8.4%); we assume +1%. FY28-29: market growth ~11-12% plus some help from IDBI Bank bancassurance if the Fairfax transfer completes; we stay below the 16-17% Emkay assumes.
assumptions._ratioWhy: FY27 calibrated to the Q1 run-rate (Q1 combined ratio 112.3%, loss ratio 73.3%, expense ratio 39%) with modest H2 relief from OD corrective actions and the DAC unwind. Loss ratio ~72-73% (in line with peers). Expense ratio falls slowly under EoM pressure but stays well above ICICI Lombard (~31%). Combined ratio 111% / 109% / 107% vs Emkay 108.9% / 106.5% / 105%.

valuation._why: Cost of equity 12.6% (6.6% G-sec + beta 1.0 x 6% ERP). Book on Ind AS: FY26 Ind AS net worth ₹7,610 cr vs IGAAP ₹4,586 cr (gap = deferred acquisition costs and reserve discounting), i.e. ~₹32.7/share, grown to ~₹34.5 by Mar-27. Ind AS ROE: 17.7% in FY26 (helped by DAC build-up in a growth year); we assume 10.5% in FY27 (flat premiums, full 25% tax, management-KPI PAT already -5% in Q1), 12% FY28, 13.5% FY29, fading to a sustainable 16% - a level that requires the combined ratio to reach ~104% on IGAAP, close to ICICI Lombard today.

cover.headline: A fast-growing insurer that has not yet learned to make money from insurance, priced as if it already has
cover.lead: Go Digit built India's fastest-growing private general insurer in eight years: ₹11,294 cr of premium in FY26, 2.9% of the market and 1.67 crore policies. But it has never made an underwriting profit. For every ₹100 of premium it earns, it pays out about ₹111 in claims and costs (combined ratio 110.7% in FY26, 112.3% in Q1FY27), and all of its profit comes from investing the float. Its costs are the second-highest of 27 general insurers, 40.5% of premium against a regulatory cap of 30%. At ₹{{P.last|num}} the market is pricing Go Digit as if it will permanently earn a ~{{dcf.impliedRoe|pct0}} return on equity (on the more generous Ind AS accounts), above what ICICI Lombard, the best-run listed peer, earns today. We see no evidence it will get there. **Initiate with SELL and a target price of {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).**

arguments.h: The business loses money on insurance; investments carry the profit
arguments.p: In FY26 Go Digit lost ₹866 cr on underwriting and earned ₹1,591 cr on investments. Its claims ratio (~73%) is in line with peers. The problem is costs: commissions and operating expenses take ~38% of premium vs ~31% at ICICI Lombard. The "digital means low cost" story is not visible in the numbers.

arguments.h: Growth has stalled and market share is slipping
arguments.p: Premiums fell 8.4% in Q1FY27, the first market-share loss since inception (motor share 6.25% → 5.6%). Management calls it deliberate ("soft by choice"), but it also shows Go Digit lacks pricing power in a competitive market. We forecast premiums flat in FY27.

arguments.h: Two sets of accounts tell different stories
arguments.p: Under the old Indian rules (IGAAP) FY26 profit was ₹544 cr and ROE 12.6%. Under the new Ind AS rules it was ₹764 cr and ROE 17.7%, mainly because commissions on multi-year policies are spread over time. We value the company on the fairer Ind AS book, and it still looks expensive.

arguments.h: The Fairfax–IDBI Bank move is the one genuine positive
arguments.p: Fairfax is acquiring ~61% of IDBI Bank and plans to move its Go Digit stake under the bank. That could give Go Digit a captive bank channel. It is not yet approved, and in our view one bank partner does not fix a cost problem. Our bull case ({{scen.bull.tp|inr}}) assumes it works and costs fall to ICICI Lombard levels; even then the upside is only {{scen.bull.upside|chg}}.

sections.title: Indian general insurance: a large, growing market where most players lose money on insurance

blocks.p: Indian general insurers collected ₹3.36 lakh crore of direct premium (GDPI) in FY26, up 9.3% (about 11% without the 1/n accounting change). Premiums have compounded at ~12% a year since FY15. India is badly under-insured: non-life premium is ~1% of GDP and US$25 per person, against a world average of 4.3% and US$555.

pair.source: GI Council, IRDAI, CareEdge, ICRA, GAM Research

pair.title: India is one of the least-insured large economies

blocks.p: The catch: **the industry as a whole loses money on insurance.** The combined ratio (claims plus costs as % of premium) was 113% in FY26, an underwriting loss of ₹45,279 cr, covered by investment income. Only a handful of players (ICICI Lombard, Bajaj General, and health specialists Star Health and Niva Bupa) run close to or below 100%. Go Digit is better than the industry average but clearly worse than the leaders.

blocks.h: What is changing in the industry

bullets: **Health is the growth engine** (~41% of premium). Standalone health insurers went from 7.9% to 13.7% market share in five years. Go Digit has only ~18% of its premium in health.
**Motor is in a volume up-cycle** (car sales +28% in H1FY27 after the GST cut), but the motor third-party tariff has not been raised since June 2022 while claim costs keep rising.

**Expense rules are tightening.** IRDAI has proposed cutting allowed expenses by about a third from January 2027 and capping commissions. That helps low-cost insurers and hurts broker-dependent, high-cost ones like Go Digit.
**100% foreign ownership is now allowed** (Insurance Laws Amendment Act, Dec-2025), which opens the door to more well-funded foreign entrants. A composite (life + non-life) licence was not included.
**Ind AS accounting** (similar to global IFRS 17) is mandatory from April 2026. It recognises costs and revenue more evenly and will change how every insurer reports profit.

sections.title: From start-up to listed insurer in eight years

blocks.p: Go Digit was founded in 2016 by Kamesh Goyal (formerly of Allianz and Bajaj Allianz) with backing from Prem Watsa's Fairfax Financial. It sold through brokers and point-of-sale agents (POSPs) using a technology-first operating model, and grew from nothing to ~₹11,300 cr of premium. It listed in May 2024 at ₹272; the stock is now around that level after peaking at ~₹398.

sections.title: Two-thirds motor, sold mostly through brokers

blocks.p: Motor insurance (own damage, OD, plus mandatory third-party, TP) is ~60% of Go Digit's gross premium and ~69% of direct premium. Health, travel and personal accident are ~18%, and fire/property ~10%. Brokers bring in 58% of direct premium and POSP agents another 13%; the company's own direct channel is ~12% and bank partners just 1%.

pair.title: Premium mix: motor-heavy, health under-weight
pair.source: Company disclosures (investor presentations, IRDAI public disclosures), GAM Research

pair.title: Channel mix: broker-dependent, almost no bank distribution

blocks.callout: **Our view:** ICICI Lombard (ICICI Bank), HDFC Ergo (HDFC Bank) and SBI General (SBI) each own a captive bank channel with low acquisition costs. Go Digit rents its customers from brokers, which is why its commission and expense ratios are structurally higher. The IDBI Bank plan addresses this only partly and only in future.

sections.title: Underwriting: claims are fine, costs are not

blocks.p: An insurer's core profit is premium earned minus claims and costs. Go Digit's **loss ratio** (claims as % of earned premium) has been 70-73% for three years, in line with ICICI Lombard (70.7%) and better than the industry (81%). Its **expense ratio** (commissions plus operating costs as % of net premium) has been 36-40%, well above the leaders. Add them up and the **combined ratio** has stayed at 107-113% every year.

pair.title: Combined ratio = loss ratio + expense ratio
Underwriting loss every year; widening again in FY27

exhibit.title: Quarterly combined ratio: no sustained improvement
exhibit.source: Company disclosures (investor presentations, IRDAI public disclosures), GAM Research

blocks.p: **What management says:** the expense ratio is inflated by IGAAP accounting. On multi-year two-wheeler policies, the full commission is expensed upfront while premium is earned over five years; this cost ~2-4 points of combined ratio in recent quarters. A further ~2 points come from the 1/n rule. On its preferred measure (combined ratio on earned premium, with deferred acquisition costs), FY26 was 105.7%. We accept part of this, but even 105-106% is worse than ICICI Lombard's 103% on a like-for-like IGAAP basis.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** Go Digit's claims discipline is adequate. Its cost base is the problem, and that is structural: broker commissions, high-acquisition-cost multi-year motor policies, and no bank channel. The regulator's expense cap (30%) is a ceiling Go Digit has breached every year.

sections.title: The investment book: where the profit really comes from

blocks.p: Insurers collect premiums before they pay claims. The money held in the meantime, the **float**, is invested. Go Digit's investment assets were ₹22,922 cr at FY26 (about 5x its net worth), earning ~7.4%. That produced ₹1,591 cr of investment income, enough to cover the ₹866 cr underwriting loss and leave a profit.

pair.title: Investment income: rising with the float
Investment assets: ~5x net worth

blocks.callout: **Why this matters:** a business that relies on investment income for 100%+ of profit is effectively a leveraged bond-and-equity portfolio with an insurance operation attached. Its earnings move with interest rates and markets. FY26 showed this: unrealised losses of ₹692 cr hit other comprehensive income when bond yields rose, and in Q1FY27 management chose not to book equity gains. A 1% lower yield would cut pre-tax profit by roughly ₹230 cr, about a quarter of FY27E PBT.

sections.title: Two sets of accounts: IGAAP vs Ind AS

blocks.p: Indian insurers moved to Ind AS (similar to global IFRS 17) from April 2026. Go Digit has regulatory permission to keep IGAAP statutory books until March 2027 but already publishes Ind AS figures, and leads its investor communication with them. The difference is large.

blocks.p: **Which is right?** Ind AS is the better economic picture: a commission paid today on a five-year policy should be spread over five years. But two cautions apply. First, in a growth phase deferred costs build up and flatter profit; when growth slows (as now) they unwind and profit growth slows. Second, cash is the same under both: the commissions have already been paid. We therefore value Go Digit on the Ind AS book (being fair to the company), but on a conservative Ind AS ROE path because FY26's 17.7% was helped by rapid DAC build-up in a growth year.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: Go Digit does not have a durable one

blocks.p: We tested every claimed advantage against data. The honest conclusion: **Go Digit does not have a durable competitive advantage.** Its technology and claims service are competent but not measurably better than incumbents. Its costs are higher, not lower. It has no captive distribution. What it does have is a strong, patient capital sponsor (Fairfax) and conservative reserving, which are real strengths but not moats.

blocks.title: Downside risks

blocks.callout: **What you would be buying:** a well-capitalised, founder-led challenger with conservative reserves, a strong sponsor (Fairfax), a long industry runway and a possible bank channel via IDBI. It has grown fast and its claims discipline is sound.

**What you would actually be paying for:** a sustainable ~19-20% return on equity that Go Digit has never earned, from a business that loses money on every ₹100 of insurance it writes, has the second-highest costs in the industry, is breaching the regulator's expense cap, has just started losing market share, and whose earnings estimates have been cut every month for a year.

bullets: **Rating: SELL, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** We see better risk-reward in ICICI Lombard, which already earns the returns Go Digit is priced for, at a lower price-to-book.

**Existing holders:** we would exit or reduce. The bull case ({{scen.bull.tp|inr}}, {{scen.bull.upside|chg}}) needs everything to go right; the bear case is {{scen.bear.tp|inr}} ({{scen.bear.upside|chg}}).
**What would make us change our mind:** a combined ratio below 105% for two consecutive quarters, the expense ratio inside the regulatory cap, or an open offer from the Fairfax–IDBI restructuring.
**Price at which we would turn neutral:** around ₹200 (≈2.2x Ind AS book), where a 17-18% long-run ROE would be fairly priced.

What it means

NWP as a % of GWP: how much risk the insurer keeps.
Claims incurred as a % of earned premium.
Commissions plus operating expenses as a % of net written premium.
Loss ratio + expense ratio. Below 100% = profit from insurance; above 100% = loss, covered by investment income.
Profit or loss from insurance itself, before investment income.
Premiums collected but not yet paid out as claims; invested in the meantime.
Available capital as a multiple of the regulatory minimum (minimum 1.5x).
IRDAI limit on commissions and operating costs as a % of premium (currently 30% for general insurers).

Own damage (cover for the customer's vehicle) and third party (mandatory liability cover, price set by the government).
Old Indian insurance accounting vs the new standard (similar to IFRS 17) mandatory from Apr-2026; Ind AS defers acquisition costs and discounts reserves.
Commissions and costs of selling a policy, spread over the policy term under Ind AS rather than expensed upfront.
How actual claims compare with the reserves set aside earlier; favourable = reserves were more than enough.
Net profit as a % of shareholders' equity.

Book value plus the present value of future profits above the cost of equity.
Share price divided by book value per share.
Selling insurance through a bank's branches and customers.

moatEvidence.evidence: FY26 EoM/GDP: Digit 40.47% (2nd worst of 27 general insurers) vs ICICI Lombard 31.70%, HDFC Ergo 31.91%, Tata AIG 31.00%, Bajaj Allianz 27.99%, SBI General 27.22%; Acko 38.69%. Cap is 30%. Q1FY27 expense ratio 39% (Emkay). 'Digital = low cost' claim not borne out.
Digit IGAAP CoR 107.4% FY23, 108.7% FY24, 109.3% FY25, 110.7% FY26, 112.4% Q1FY27 - deteriorating. ICICI Lombard FY26 CoR 103.4% (1/n) / 102.4% (n). Digit's underwriting loss Rs866cr FY26.
Net loss ratio 72.8% FY25, 72.9% FY26, 73.3% Q1FY27 (Motor OD rising) - in line with large private peers; underwriting gap comes from expenses, not claims.

Company claims: manual policy issuance 0.37%, 40.6 lakh digitally-enabled claims since inception, CSAT 95.7% motor / 83.3% non-motor, 82.9% health cashless approvals <30 min, ~1mn claims settled FY26. No independent peer benchmark; incumbents (ICICI Lombard etc.) have comparable digital stacks. Advantage unproven.

FY26 NL-45: 3,321 complaints; 21.69 claim complaints per 10,000 claims; ~0.53 policy complaints per 10,000 policies on 1.67cr policies. Industry general+health: 5.29 grievances per lakh policies FY25. No like-for-like peer data retrieved.

81,124 partners (Mar-26) - intermediary/agent/POSP/OEM dependent with no captive bank, unlike ICICI Lombard (ICICI Bank), HDFC Ergo (HDFC Bank), SBI General; high commission ratio (~29% Q1FY27). Potential change: IDBI Bank bancassurance if Fairfax transfer completes.
88 active products, but Motor = 69% of FY26 GDP (CRISIL) vs more diversified ICICI Lombard/Bajaj; market share 3.4% total / 6.3% motor (FY26), motor share fell to 5.6% in Q1FY27.
Consistent favourable development (Motor TP 22-41% for AY20-23; ex-TP 6-13%).
Solvency 2.42x FY26 / 2.43x Q1FY27; Fairfax moving to 57% direct and can go to 100% under new FDI law; CRISIL lists rising Fairfax stake as upside trigger.
No independent brand-strength data found; brand owned by promoter-group Go Digit Solutions and licensed in. Celebrity investor association (Kohli) is marketing, not moat.
GWP 11,294cr FY26 (+10%), GDP +16%, but Q1FY27 GWP -8.4% YoY and first market-share loss; ICICI Lombard GDPI 28,712cr FY26 is ~2.9x Digit.

critiques.point: No clear moat; IPO priced richly - initiated Sell with ~31% downside at listing; stayed Sell/Reduce throughout; now cites high-opex model and competitive intensity.

Combined ratio >100% every year (107-111%); profits rely on investment income (Rs1,591cr) to offset underwriting deficit (Rs866cr); expense ratio 35-40%; profitability to stay constrained near-medium term.
Serial breach of IRDAI expense-of-management limits (40.47% vs 30% in FY26) - regulatory and structural cost problem.
Q1FY27: CoR worsened to 112.3%, U/W loss +46% to Rs282cr; near-term outlook challenging until motor corrective actions work.
Growth slowing and share being lost: GWP -8.4% YoY in Q1FY27, first market-share decline since inception; motor share 6.25% -> 5.6%.
Expensive vs industry P/B; analysts downgrading forward EPS (FY27 EPS -17.5% in 12 months).
Bear narrative: rising climate risks and costly competition will impair margins; bear TP Rs270.
Headline Ind AS CoR (99.1% Q4FY26) flatters vs IGAAP (111.6%) via reserve discounting and DAC deferral - optics, not economics.

Promoter-group reinsurer (Valueattics) now receiving cessions and ceding business back to Digit - related-party flows rising sharply (Q1FY27 inward premium Rs47cr vs nil).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Go Digit General Insurance (standalone, IGAAP, ₹ crore). Base year FY26A from company disclosures. Valuation on Ind AS book (fairer economics) via residual income.
assumptions._gwpWhy: FY27: management is 'soft by choice' and prepared for flat-to-negative growth until Mar-27 (Q1 GWP -8.4%); we assume +1%. FY28-29: market growth ~11-12% plus some help from IDBI Bank bancassurance if the Fairfax transfer completes; we stay below the 16-17% Emkay assumes.
assumptions._ratioWhy: FY27 calibrated to the Q1 run-rate (Q1 combined ratio 112.3%, loss ratio 73.3%, expense ratio 39%) with modest H2 relief from OD corrective actions and the DAC unwind. Loss ratio ~72-73% (in line with peers). Expense ratio falls slowly under EoM pressure but stays well above ICICI Lombard (~31%). Combined ratio 111% / 109% / 107% vs Emkay 108.9% / 106.5% / 105%.

valuation._why: Cost of equity 12.6% (6.6% G-sec + beta 1.0 x 6% ERP). Book on Ind AS: FY26 Ind AS net worth ₹7,610 cr vs IGAAP ₹4,586 cr (gap = deferred acquisition costs and reserve discounting), i.e. ~₹32.7/share, grown to ~₹34.5 by Mar-27. Ind AS ROE: 17.7% in FY26 (helped by DAC build-up in a growth year); we assume 10.5% in FY27 (flat premiums, full 25% tax, management-KPI PAT already -5% in Q1), 12% FY28, 13.5% FY29, fading to a sustainable 16% - a level that requires the combined ratio to reach ~104% on IGAAP, close to ICICI Lombard today.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Indian general insurers: one-year-forward P/E on Indian GAAP EPS (ICICI Lombard 28-30x, Star Health 22-29x, Go Digit 31-35x at HDFC Sec / Emkay-implied). 25x = ~15% discount to ICICI Lombard for half its ROE and no underwriting profit; bull 32x (street level), bear 18x.

methods.name: Residual income
methods.why: Intrinsic value on Ind AS book and sustainable ROE (Emkay uses the same approach).

methods.name: P/B
methods.why: Book-value check: ICICI Lombard ~5.5x on ~19% ROE; 3.5x for Go Digit's ~12-14% ROE.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: IDBI Bank bancassurance takes off, the motor TP tariff is finally raised, and costs fall to ICICI Lombard levels - long-run ROE reaches ~20%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Soft pricing persists, costs stay ~38% of premium, motor TP claims inflation bites after the Shishupal ruling - long-run ROE stalls near the cost of equity.
